verifications.claim: NASA launched the Artemis II mission at 6:35 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' (6:36 PM / April 1, 2026); R3: 'At 6:35 p.m. ET...'; R4: 'At 6:35 p.m. ET this evening'; R6: 'lift off... at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact launch time and date as 6:35 p.m. EDT/ET on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launch was successful.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Post-launch updates (e.g., 'Artemis II lifts off', core stage separates, etc.); R3: 'History has been made... successful liftoff'; R4: 'The SLS did not so much lift from its pad as vault from it'; R6: 'We have a liftoff!'
verifications.reasoning: All sources report the launch occurred successfully with no scrubs and post-liftoff milestones achieved.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center'; R4: 'pad 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'; R6: 'Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Every source explicitly confirms Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is Space Launch System (SLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R2: 'NASA's giant Space Launch System rocket'; R3: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R4: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) moon rocket'; R6: 'Space Launch System rocket'
verifications.reasoning: All sources identify SLS as the launch vehicle.

verifications.claim: The launch site for the Artemis II mission is Launch Complex 39B, Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Complex 39B'; R2: 'Launch Complex 39B'; R3: 'Pad 39B'; R4: 'pad 39B'; R6: 'Launch Pad 39B'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently specify LC-39B/Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket for the Artemis II mission was crewed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch'; R2: 'first one carrying astronauts to space'; R3: 'SLS rocket... carrying the Orion spacecraft and its crew'; R4: 'carrying its four-person Artemis II crew'; R6: 'NASA’s Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft carrying... crew'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS carried crew for Artemis II, its first crewed flight.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lifted off on a 10-day journey around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days' (close to 10); R2: '10-day journey around the moon'; R3: '10-day mission around the moon'; R4: '10-day journey around the far side'; R5: '10-day moon mission'; R6: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe ~10-day mission looping/flying around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first human mission to the lunar vicinity in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since... Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'first time since 1972'; R3: 'first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years'; R4: 'first time... since Apollo 17... 1972'; R6: 'first crewed moon mission since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (1972), over 50 years prior to 2026.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; identical in R2-R6
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly these four as the crew.

verifications.claim: The mission goal of the Artemis II mission is a 10-day flight around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it... 24 hours orbiting Earth... four-day journey to... moon and another four days back'; R2: '10-day journey around the moon and back'; R3: '10-day mission around the moon'; R4: '10-day journey around the far side of the moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 10-day flyby/loop around moon and return.

verifications.claim: The initial target time for the Artemis II mission was 6:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch window opens at 6:24 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'two-hour window starting at 6:24 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'opening of the launch window at 6:24 p.m. ET'; R5: '6:24 p.m. ET'; R6: '6:24 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state initial window/target as 6:24 p.m. ET/EDT.

verifications.claim: The target time for the Artemis II mission was adjusted slightly to 6:35 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:31 PM... "go" for launch... 6:36 PM... lifted off at 6:35 p.m.'; R3: 'adjusted to 6:35 p.m. ET, moving slightly deeper into the two-hour window'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states adjustment from initial window to 6:35; R1 timeline shows shift from 6:24 window to actual 6:35.
